description: A small e-commerce estate whose most stealable asset is not data but value: loyalty points, convertible to gift cards through a partner. The theft is a business-logic path rather than a malware path, and its central control is separation of duties - an adjustment above the threshold needs an agent to raise it and a supervisor to approve it, so the attacker must hold two accounts with different roles. Planted findings: customer MFA is optional, the agent console can adjust points below the threshold without any second party, notification suppression is available to agents and barely logged, and the strongest detections are not security tools at all - a vendor fraud engine, a nightly points-liability reconciliation, the partner's daily settlement file and customers complaining that their points are missing.

zones.name: Back office
zones.description: Agent and supervisor tooling used by staff.

zones.name: Finance enclave
zones.description: Systems of record for monetary and near-monetary balances.

zones.name: Partner services
zones.description: Third parties: fraud scoring, mail delivery and gift-card redemption.

components.name: Storefront
components.description: Public shop. Customers see their points balance and redeem here.

controls.name: Bot management
controls.description: Rate limits login attempts per address. Ineffective against a low-and-slow credential stuffing run from residential proxies.

components.name: Customer identity service
components.description: Customer accounts. MFA is offered and rarely enabled.

controls.name: Optional customer MFA
controls.description: Available, opted into by a small minority. Marketing resists making it mandatory at checkout.

components.name: Agent console
components.description: Customer service tooling. Agents can look up any customer, adjust points below the approval threshold and suppress outbound notifications while they work a ticket.

controls.name: Role-based agent permissions
controls.description: Agent and supervisor roles are distinct, but several long-serving agents hold both for holiday cover.

controls.name: Session recording of agent actions
controls.description: Records screens for quality assurance. Reviewed by sampling, for tone rather than fraud.

components.name: Supervisor approval console
components.description: Where an adjustment above the threshold is approved. The second half of the separation of duties control.

controls.name: Hardware key required for approval
controls.description: Phishing-resistant. Taking this account needs the key itself or a session on an already-trusted device.
bypass_requirements: theft of a registered security key
session hijack on an approved workstation

controls.name: Approval queue review
controls.description: Supervisors clear a queue under handling-time pressure; approvals that look routine are rarely questioned.

components.name: Loyalty ledger
components.description: System of record for point balances and adjustments. Points are a monetary liability and convert to gift cards.

controls.name: Dual approval above 5,000 points
controls.description: Separation of duties. One account raises the adjustment, a second with the supervisor role approves it. Enforced in the application, not the database, and only above the threshold.
bypass_requirements: compromise of a second account holding the approver role
or splitting the theft into adjustments below the threshold

controls.name: Immutable adjustment audit log
controls.description: Every adjustment is written with actor, approver, reason code and prior balance. Rich evidence that nothing currently alerts on.

controls.name: Nightly points liability reconciliation
controls.description: Finance compares issued, redeemed and expired points against the liability account. A business process, not a security tool, and the control most likely to notice the aggregate.
bypass_requirements: keeping daily totals inside normal variance

components.name: Order database
components.description: Orders, addresses and contact details. Useful to an attacker for picking dormant high-balance accounts.

components.name: Vendor fraud scoring engine
components.description: Scores redemption and adjustment events and raises anomaly alerts. Its alerts do not correspond to any ATT&CK technique.

controls.name: Velocity and anomaly rules
controls.description: Vendor-tuned. Catches bursts; a patient attacker below the velocity threshold is invisible to it.
bypass_requirements: redemptions spread across accounts and days

controls.name: Model drift review
controls.description: Quarterly vendor review of scoring quality. Nobody internal can explain a score.

components.name: Transactional email provider
components.description: Sends the 'points redeemed' and 'balance changed' notifications that would otherwise tell the customer first.

controls.name: Notification suppression logging
controls.description: Agents may suppress notifications while working a ticket. The suppression is recorded in the provider, not in the ledger, and the two are never joined.

components.name: Gift card redemption partner
components.description: Converts points to gift card codes. Where stolen points become money and leave the estate.

controls.name: Daily settlement file
controls.description: The partner sends a daily file of redemptions. Reconciled weekly by one analyst, so the earliest external evidence arrives up to a week late.

controls.name: Per-account redemption velocity cap
bypass_requirements: spreading redemption across many customer accounts

components.name: Customer complaints queue
components.description: Where 'my points are missing' arrives. In loyalty fraud this is frequently the first true detection, and it is owned by customer service rather than security.

controls.name: Complaint triage SLA
controls.description: Tickets are triaged for satisfaction, not correlated. Ten identical complaints in a week look like ten unhappy customers.

flows.description: Agent adjustments. Below the threshold this needs no second party.
Customer lookup, including dormancy and balance history.
Approval of an adjustment above the threshold. The second half of separation of duties.
Adjustment and redemption events submitted for scoring.
Points converted to gift card codes.
Complaints become tickets an agent works - including, in this scenario, the complaints the attacker's own activity generates.
